title: Whose Preferences? Differences in Fairness Preferences and Their Impact on the Fairness of AI Utilizing Human Feedback
findings: The sensitive attribute mentioned in sentence pairs, including religion, significantly impacts annotators' fairness judgments. Compared to sentence pairs where the sensitive attribute was race, pairs differing by religion were slightly less likely to be judged as deserving different treatment when annotators predicted the average American's opinion (Odds ratio 0.91, p=0.02). The effect on annotators' personal opinions was not statistically significant.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures human annotators' fairness preferences for pairs of sentences that differ along a sensitive attribute, including religion. Specifically, it assesses whether two semantically similar, often toxic, comments referencing different religious groups should receive the same treatment from a content moderator.
